ci: enforce the Rust toolchain pin instead of asking for it in a comment (#1010)

* ci: enforce the rust toolchain pin instead of asking for it in a comment

The pin itself already shipped and is correct: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
1.97.1, and both `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` uses are pinned to the SHA for that
same version. What was missing is any enforcement.

The two halves cannot reference each other — that action does not read toolchain
files, its `@rev` IS the version selector — so the only thing tying them
together was a comment in three files saying "bump both together". That is the
shape this repo treats as a defect: a stated invariant with nothing checking it.

The failure is quiet, which is what makes it worth a check. Bump the TOML alone
and CI keeps building on the old compiler; bump the action alone and every
developer's machine drifts off what CI validates. Neither goes red on its own —
the pin simply stops meaning anything, which is exactly the state it was created
to end.

`scripts/check-toolchain-pin.mjs` asserts four things: the channel is an exact
three-part version rather than a floating one; every `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`
use under `.github/` carries a trailing `# <version>` comment (an opaque SHA is
unreviewable by construction, so the comment is load-bearing, not decoration);
every one of those declared versions equals the channel; and the Cargo MSRV is
not above the pin, since that pairing cannot compile at all.

It deliberately does NOT verify that the SHA truly is that version — that needs
a network call, and it is not the mistake people make. The realistic error is
updating one place and forgetting the other, which is fully catchable offline.

Wired into the `lint-format` job, which has no path filter and so runs on every
PR — a toolchain drift guard that only fires when Rust files change would miss
the case where someone edits only the workflow. The three comments now name
their enforcer instead of asking nicely.

Guard is mutation-tested five ways against the real repo (bump either half
alone, float the channel back to `stable`, strip a version comment, raise the
MSRV past the pin) — all red, tree restored clean — plus 11 black-box CLI tests
over a fake repo tree, following `check-tech-radar.test.mjs`. One of those
covers removing CI's pin entirely, which would otherwise pass vacuously: with
nothing to compare, nothing disagrees.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): reject a moving action ref, not just a mismatched version comment

CodeRabbit on #1010, and it is the same hole as the one this guard was written
to close.

The check validated the `# <version>` comment beside each
`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@<rev>` and never the rev itself, so
`uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable # 1.97.1` passed. A moving ref defeats the
pin exactly the way a `stable` channel does — and arguably worse, because the
comment beside it is then a claim nothing keeps true: the action can re-point at
a different compiler with no diff in this repo at all. I checked the channel for
floating and forgot the other half.

The test helper defaulted every rev to `deadbeef` — eight characters — and all
11 tests passed, which is the same blind spot expressed twice. It now uses a
real 40-hex SHA, and there are regressions for `@stable`, `@main`, `@v1`,
`@master` and a truncated SHA, each with a MATCHING version comment so they fail
on the rev rather than incidentally on the comment.

Verified both directions: pointing the real repo's action at `@stable` goes red,
and removing the SHA check turns two tests red.

fix(locale): give Spain, Portugal and Brazil the profiles they were already promised (#1009)

* fix(locale): give spain, portugal and brazil the profiles they were already promised

#1007 fixed Italy and explicitly deferred the identical gap for Spain and
Portugal. This closes it, and Brazil with it.

All three were already live market ids on the TS side — `COUNTRY_TO_MARKET`
maps `ES`/`PT`/`BR` and `LANGUAGE_TO_MARKET` maps `es`/`pt` — and the Rust side
had an arm for none of them, so they fell through to the international default.
The visible result was half a localization: `resume_conventions` HAS curated
es/pt entries, so the model wrote "Experiencia profesional" and "Formação" and
then arranged them in the American order, with `photo: Never` and the 2-page
Anglophone budget. Half-localized reads worse than not localized, because the
document then matches no market's expectations.

`IT_ORDER` is renamed `EUROPASS_ORDER` and now serves all four. That is what it
always was — the doc already justified it by pointing at Europass, not at
anything specifically Italian.

Scope is principled, not arbitrary: these are exactly the markets whose section
HEADINGS are already curated. A market with no curated headings (tr, ru, cn, jp,
kr are all live TS ids too) gets English headings, and giving it a non-English
section ORDER would create the same half-localized document this commit is
fixing. The order axis tracks the heading axis deliberately.

Two per-market calls, both flagged as reviewable rather than asserted:

- Spain and Portugal cap at **2 pages**, not Italy's 3. Spanish guidance is
  consistently "máximo dos páginas", and this cap is advice the trim panel acts
  on, so inheriting 3 would license a longer document than the market expects.
- Brazil gets `photo: Never` where Portugal gets `Optional` — Brazilian hiring
  guidance has moved against CV photos on anti-discrimination grounds. Same
  language and same section order, different norm; that is precisely why it is
  a distinct profile rather than an alias.

`all_markets_are_distinct_and_present` asserted a hardcoded count and id list,
so it could not have caught any of this — it passed throughout. It now asserts
the property instead: every profile `all()` advertises must round-trip through
`get()` back to itself. Mutation-checked by deleting the `"es"` arm, which is
the exact shape of the bug that shipped; the old test stayed green under it.

Every guard here mutation-checked: green at baseline, red with the feature
deleted, restored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(locale): reattach italy's doc to italy, and stop claiming the page cap is enforced

CodeRabbit flagged a contradiction on #1009: the Spain profile said the page cap
is "advice the export actually enforces", while `max_pages`'s own field doc says
it is advisory and that nothing blocks a longer export. The field doc is right,
and it predates this branch.

Chasing it found the actual cause, which the finding described only as a
symptom. The new constructors were inserted at the wrong offset — between
Italy's doc comment and `pub fn it()`. Rust attaches a doc comment to whatever
item follows it, so **Italy's documentation had silently become Spain's**, and
`it()` was left with none. That is why two page-limit paragraphs ended up
adjacent and disagreeing: they were never meant to be read together.

Moved the three constructors below `it()`, restoring the original attachment,
and reworded the Spain note to state what actually happens: inheriting Italy's
3 would not break an export, it would stop the trim panel ever offering a
suggestion to a Spanish user whose CV has run a page long.

Also finishes the `IT_ORDER` → `EUROPASS_ORDER` rename — three doc references
in `locale/mod.rs` and `pipeline/resume/test.rs` still named the old const.
Nothing failed, because a doc comment naming a symbol that no longer exists
compiles perfectly well; that is precisely the class this repo treats as a
defect rather than a nit.

feat(scraping): add freehire as the aggregator's keyless tier (#1008)

* feat(scraping): add freehire as the aggregator's keyless tier

Issue #1002, opened by freehire's maintainer, who disclosed the interest. We
publicly committed to shipping it in the next release.

Implemented from their published openapi.yaml rather than from the PR they
offered. The reason is rights, not code quality: this repo has no CLA, so a
contribution stays under its author's copyright and cannot be relicensed, and
ADR-023 names commercial licensing as a rationale. Reading their PR and
rewriting it would be derivative — the worst of both worlds — so the spec is
the only source used.

What it buys: every other provider needs an API key, so a fresh install gets a
needs-keys skip and zero jobs. freehire answers unauthenticated, so the
aggregator board can return results before the user has configured anything.
It is not a better source than the keyed tiers and is never preferred over
one — it runs LAST, after Adzuna, JSearch and Jooble have each failed to
produce a decisive result, and only a non-empty answer from it short-circuits.
An empty answer from a provider nobody chose is not evidence about the search,
so it must not swallow a configured provider's failure diagnostic.

Two consequences worth calling out rather than burying:

`needs_keys()` is now always false, because a keyless tier is always
"configured". That is the point — the skip existed because a keyless search
could only ever return nothing. The cost, accepted and tested: a keyless user
whose freehire search finds nothing reads "no jobs found" rather than a prompt
to add keys. A keyring READ FAULT is still classified separately, so the one
case the old `false` protected is unaffected.

Failures degrade to Ok(empty), never Err — the only provider with that rule.
Every other one reports its failure because a stored key means the user asked
for it specifically. Nobody opted into this one, so surfacing its outage would
turn a third party's downtime into an error banner on a search the user never
aimed at them. There is no SLA and no rate-limit header of any kind (verified:
no X-RateLimit-*, no Retry-After), so it is treated as always-possibly-absent.

Uses the documented /agent/jobs/search with `q` and
`description_format=markdown` — NOT the undocumented /jobs/search taking
`query`, which is what the issue described and what a first pass reached for;
building from the published spec is the whole basis for implementing this
ourselves. Markdown up front is also what keeps scoring from needing a
per-result detail fetch.

A guessed country is deliberately not sent as a filter: the aggregator defaults
`country` to "de" when the caller supplied none, and pinning a keyless tier to
that guess would reproduce the guessed-market bug already fixed for Adzuna.
`location` is unused because the documented search has no city parameter at
all, and folding a city into the full-text `q` would drop every posting that
does not spell its city out, remote ones included.

Egress: freehire.me is in the inventory with a public_name, which made the
landing drift guard fail until the privacy page, README and SECURITY named it.
That guard shipped two PRs ago for exactly this, and this is the first new
egress since — it worked.

Every behaviour above is pinned by a test that was mutation-checked: green at
baseline, red with the feature deleted, restored. The one claim that did not
survive checking is recorded in the test rather than quietly dropped — the
ordering guard catches "moved ahead of the keyed tiers" but would NOT catch
"moved one rung up past Jooble", because the fixture short-circuits at Adzuna.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): stop the keyless tier from masking what it must not mask

Pre-PR review reproduced two regressions of existing guards. Both are mine and
both came from the same mistake: treating an always-on provider as if it were
just one more tier, when "always on" is exactly what makes it able to hide
things.

**It replaced the sparse guessed-market hits instead of merging with them.**
Reproduced in the commonest real configuration — Adzuna-only keys, no country
supplied, a real location: two London-relevant Adzuna hits were discarded for
up to fifty globally-unfiltered freehire ones. That is the guessed-market bug
this repo already fixed for Adzuna, re-entered through a new door. It now
merges, sparse hits first so dedupe's first-seen-wins order preserves them.

The comment justifying the original behaviour claimed "the free-text location
still reaches `q`, so a real place name is not lost". That was false, and I
made it false myself: the sentence was written before I removed `location`
from the function on discovering the API has no city parameter at all. On a
guessed market this tier is location-blind, which is precisely why it must not
replace hits that are not.

**It swallowed every configured provider's failure diagnostic.** Reproduced:
three revoked keys, and `BoardScrapeSummary.error` came back `None`. Since
`needs_keys()` is now permanently false, no surface anywhere in the app would
have told the user their key was broken — indefinitely. It is now skipped
whenever a configured provider actually failed.

That guard was wrong on its first attempt too, and the test caught it: the
guessed-market branch records its fall-through in `adzuna_configured_failed`,
so a naive `is_some()` check read a routing decision as a key failure and
switched the tier off in the one case it is most useful. Split into a distinct
`adzuna_distrusted_a_guessed_market` flag.

Also from the review:

- The privacy page said freehire runs after every keyed tier "has come back
  empty or failed". A keyed tier's `Ok(empty)` is decisive and returns
  immediately, so that was a false statement on a public disclosure page. Now
  "is unconfigured or has failed". The drift guard could not catch this — it
  checks that a named host appears, not that the claim around it is true.
- `freehire_slugless_rows_key_off_their_url_not_each_other` asserted only
  pairwise inequality and stayed GREEN when the reviewer mutated the fallback
  id to a non-deterministic counter — a change that would break cross-run
  dedupe and resurface every slugless posting as new on each re-scrape. It now
  asserts the concrete value. This is the repo's recorded pass-for-the-wrong-
  reason shape and I reproduced it in my own new test.
- `description` now goes through `html_to_markdown` like every sibling
  provider. The "already markdown, no conversion needed" rationale was wrong
  in both directions: the call is free (it early-returns tag-free input
  verbatim) and it is the only defence when freehire's upstreams leave HTML in
  a field labelled markdown.
- Stale contract docs the change invalidated: the aggregator module header
  still described a three-provider chain and claimed "none configured →
  keyless-empty"; `Scraper::needs_keys` and the `boards.ts` skip contract still
  described needs-keys as live; `scraping-domain.md` omitted the tier entirely.

Three new chain tests, all mutation-checked green-at-baseline / red-with-the-
feature-deleted, including one asserting the tier still answers when nothing
failed — without it, tightening the guard to "never run" would leave both
failure-direction tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): dedupe the cross-provider merge by url, and correct two docs

All three from CodeRabbit on #1008; all three verified against the code before
acting rather than applied on sight.

**Dedupe by URL after the merge.** `dedupe` keys on `external_id`, which is
provider-prefixed, so the same job surfaced by both the sparse Adzuna tier and
freehire was two distinct keys and rendered twice. `dedupe_by_url` already
exists for exactly this and is already used on the additive Apify merge — the
freehire merge is the only OTHER cross-provider merge in `primary_chain`, so it
needed the same second pass. The single-provider path keeps `dedupe` alone,
since `canonical_url` collapsing is not wanted there. New test, mutation-checked.

**The privacy page was still wrong, in a second way.** The previous commit fixed
"empty or failed" → "unconfigured or has failed", but the same commit had also
made freehire SKIP on a configured provider's failure, so "has failed" was now
false too. It now says freehire runs only when none of the keyed tiers failed,
and says why: an erroring key shows you the error rather than being quietly
answered around. Two passes to get one sentence true is the cost of changing
behaviour and copy in the same change.

**`scraping-domain.md` is a shape-only page** — it says so in its own header —
and the freehire section had grown into a copy of the runtime contract, which is
how docs go stale. Reduced to pointers at the module doc, `primary_chain` and
ADR-0005, keeping only the one consequence that is invisible from those files:
`needs_keys()` never returns true in production any more.

fix(resume): localize every section heading, not the first four (#1007)

* fix(prompts): localize every resume section heading, not the first four

A German resume rendered "Projekte" and "Ausbildung & Sprachen" as body text
while PROFIL, BERUFSERFAHRUNG and KENNTNISSE rendered as headings.

section_order_prompt_list handed the model NINE section names as raw English
SectionId debug strings while ResumeConventions.headers localized only FOUR.
Its own doc comment admitted it. So the German prompt asked for German prose and
supplied English words for Projects, Certifications, Languages, Awards and
Publications - the model invented German names no vocabulary had heard of.
English worked by luck, because the model invents "Projects" and the parser
happens to know that word.

headers is now a total record over the nine ordered ids, so TypeScript is the
completeness guard: a new ordered section cannot ship without a name in every
locale. Removing one from the de locale fails tsc, which is the mutation check.

Two German candidates were rejected by running classify_section rather than
reasoning about it. Sprachkenntnisse classifies as Skills, so a regenerate would
rewrite the wrong section; Weiterbildung classifies as Education and collides
with Ausbildung. Sprachen and Zertifikate land in Other and collide with
nothing. locale/resume.rs's own doc comment recommended Weiterbildung - that
comment was wrong and is fixed. Every Italian heading was checked the same way.

PR #1003 reworded the section list to "an ORDER, not a checklist" to stop empty
sections, and in doing so dropped the clause forbidding merged headings. That is
where "Ausbildung & Sprachen" came from; the clause is back, without the
manifest reading #1003 removed.

Italy silently received the US section order - section_order_for had a DE arm
and nothing else. IT_ORDER puts education and certifications straight after
experience, and diverges from the German order only on Languages before Skills,
following Europass nesting language competence first. That divergence is marked
in the doc comment as the reviewable call.

section_order_prompt_list moved from locale::resume to pipeline::resume::prompts.
Localizing it there would have made an L1 module import L2; the architecture
test caught it as R7. locale::resume stays a pure order source and the order
becomes localized text one layer up.

Note draft_system interpolates its heading slots in the positional order
summary, skills, experience, education - not the order the sentence reads. A
comment now says so, because reordering them to read naturally silently
mislabels every heading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(locale): give italy a profile instead of resolving it to english

Italy was not a known region. LocaleProfile::get and is_known_region covered
us, uk, gb, de, at, ch, fr, nl, eu and dach, and recommend had no italian arm at
all, so an italian job auto-resolved to intl() - id "en", photo Never, two
pages. A4 was already right so there is no paper bug, but an italian CV may
carry a photo, Europass-style CVs run past two pages, and that "en" id is what
fed an italian user the US section order on the auto-recommend path. The
explicitly-selected market path already reached "it" correctly.

The profile is a dedicated it() rather than an alias to eu(), even though every
field is identical. The id has to stay "it": pick_locale forwards it verbatim as
the export market string and section_order_for matches the literal "it" to
select IT_ORDER, so aliasing would fix page and photo while silently handing
back the default section order - the same bug one hop downstream. That reasoning
is in the constructor's doc comment, because the fields being identical makes
"simplify this to eu()" an inviting future change.

Verified there is no italian equivalent of the DE/AT/CH-versus-dach split that
once gave german users the default order: COUNTRY_TO_MARKET["IT"] and
LANGUAGE_TO_MARKET["it"] both map to a single "it". No mirrored alias test was
added, because a test for a split that does not exist would assert nothing.

Spain and Portugal have the identical gap and are deliberately left open - both
have curated resume and letter conventions but nobody waiting on them, and
folding them in would stop this diff reading as the Italy fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): recognize the localized headings the prompt now emits

The producer half localized nine section names across seven locales; the parser
knew four English project variants and zero non-English ones. Measured before
the fix: projekte, projets, proyectos, progetti, projecten and projetos all
returned zero occurrences in SECTION_NAMES, while every other german heading was
already there - which is exactly why only Projects broke on a german resume.

The added vocabulary was derived by diffing the generated prompt_blocks header
table against SECTION_NAMES rather than transcribed from the design. Portuguese
carries both premios and premios spellings: nothing in the header table
discriminates pt-PT from pt-BR, so the recognizer accepts both while the
producer emits one.

The guard that matters is every_producer_heading_is_recognised_by_the_parser -
all nine ordered ids across all seven locales must parse as a SectionHeader.
Reverting the new entries reproduces the reported defect verbatim: `locale "de"
heading "Projekte" (for SectionId::Projects) was not recognised as a
SectionHeader by export::parser, got Text`.

Honest limit on that guard, worth recording: it works because the producer is
now a TOTAL record. Before that commit the prompt used the english Debug name
"Projects" for the five uncovered ids - a string the recognizer already knew -
so this guard run against the original code would have passed vacuously. The
historical defect was partly the model inventing a german translation of an
english placeholder inside an otherwise-german prompt, which no fixture test
predicts. The guard is the right shape for the producer-recognizer contract from
here on; it is not a claim it would have caught the original.

Combined headings are recognized, not split. is_known_section_name now accepts
"X & Y" when both halves are individually known. Splitting was rejected: there
is no reliable signal for which half later content belongs to, so a structural
split risks misattributing it - worse than one heading covering both. Real ATS
bucket by heading text and get no signal at all from a plain paragraph, so
recognizing an imperfect heading beats leaving it as prose. Prompt-side
prevention stays the primary fix; this is for documents already generated.

SectionId::from_header is deliberately NOT localized here. It is a semantic
classifier feeding reorder_sections, so a misclassification silently reorders
content - a worse failure than a heading rendering as text, and it needs the
same collision analysis the producer did for Sprachkenntnisse and Weiterbildung.
Its comment promised a "later phase" that never came; it now states the gap
plainly instead.

Blast radius covered by tests: a company named "Projekte GmbH", a bullet opening
with a section word, prose merely containing one, and a colon-labelled
"Sprachen: Deutsch" skills group all stay non-headings. The whole-line exact
match is what protects them, and it is unchanged. No golden export fixture moved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(resume): make the heading guards enumerate what they claim to enumerate

Pre-PR review found three guards on this branch that could not fail for the
reason they were written, and one live gap they were blind to.

The producer/recogniser guard's doc says a new SectionId or locale fails
HERE. It could not: both axes were literal const arrays inside the test, so
anything added on the TS side was simply never visited. The codegen now
emits `RESUME_CONVENTION_LOCALES` and `ResumeConventions::ids()`, and the
guard loops over those. Mutation: added an 8th locale to the TS conventions
with headings absent from SECTION_NAMES — red, naming it; it was green
before.

`header()` falls back to the raw English SectionId word rather than
panicking, and nothing tied the TS id union to the ids `section_order_for`
emits, so adding `SectionId::Volunteer` to an order const put the literal
word "Volunteer" in a prompt demanding Italian with every gate green. The
new guard asserts key MEMBERSHIP, not `header(id) != id` — the value
comparison reads as a fallback for French "Certifications", which is
correctly spelled the same as English. That is not hypothetical: the
inequality form failed on fr the first time it ran.

The collision sweep covered de + it by name and missed three of the four
German words this branch adds. Replacing the literal list with a locale x id
loop surfaced a live pre-existing defect: Portuguese "Competências"
classified as Other, so a pt résumé generated by this app did not recognise
its own skills section. The `ê` blocks `competenc` exactly as `z` blocked it
for Italian. First draft of the sweep allowed `want || Other` and could not
fail; every bucketed id already lands on its own bucket in all 7 locales, so
the slack bought nothing and cost the guard.

Also: `isKnownSectionName` never gained the `" & "` join arm Rust has, so
every merged heading answered false on the TS side with the section-names
fixture still green — that fixture compares two name LISTS and is
structurally blind to a rule combining two entries. Mirrored, with a shared
`section-name-joins.json` pinning the predicate on both sides, including the
three-part cases that pin `split_once`'s cut-at-the-first-separator
semantics ("certifications & training" contains a separator of its own).

Every guard above was mutation-checked: green at baseline, red with the
feature deleted, restored.

Two stale doc comments fixed: the Italy paragraph a later commit in this
same PR contradicted, and a JSDoc pointing at the pre-move location of
`section_order_prompt_list`.

refactor(platform): own the test data-dir override where the rule says it belongs (#1006)

The Stop gate flagged std::env::var in the new SSRF test. The architecture test
disagreed and passed, because R4 exempts files it classifies as tests - so the
rule was enforceable everywhere except the one place a test would actually reach
for the variable. The gate was right in spirit: platform/config.rs's own module
doc calls it the sole owner of that env var and says no other module may read
it.

Rather than argue the exemption, the override moved to where the rule points.
platform::config::DataDirGuard is a test-only RAII scope: a caller names a
directory, never the variable. It restores on Drop instead of at the end of the
test body, so a panicking assertion cannot leak the override into whatever runs
next - which the previous inline version could.

Also added #[serial] to data_dir_honors_env_then_falls_back. It mutates the same
process-global variable directly and had no serialization, so it could race the
new test. That gap was pre-existing but only became reachable once a second test
started scoping the same variable.

The test file now contains no env access and does not name the variable in
prose either, so both the gate's ast-grep matcher and R4's literal search are
satisfied for the right reason rather than by an exemption.

feat: make the egress inventory testable, and close two holes found doing it (#1005)

* fix(landing): vendor chart.js instead of loading it from a cdn

The benchmarks page loaded chart.js@2.9.2 from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no SRI,
on the same origin as the GitHub token in localStorage (see
lib/mission-control/config.ts). A compromised CDN or package could read it.

Files under apps/landing/public/ are copied verbatim by the static export, so
they never pass through ClientScripts.tsx's fail-closed isAllowedScriptSrc
guard - the invariant existed, this page just was not subject to it. CspMeta
is rendered only by the mission-control route, so no CSP covered /benchmarks/
either.

Vendored rather than pinned with an integrity hash: this change is about the
egress inventory, and deleting an origin beats documenting one. SRI would also
still leak a request to jsDelivr on every page view. The bytes were verified
against jsDelivr's own published package hash before being trusted.

The benchmark action appends to data.js and does not rewrite index.html - git
history confirms it, index.html was last written by a human commit and data.js
by the action.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(profile-import): match the linkedin host, and fetch through the ssrf guard

detect_platform tested `url.to_lowercase().contains("linkedin.com/in/")` over
the WHOLE url, so https://attacker.example/linkedin.com/in/x classified as
LinkedIn - and linkedin.rs then fetched it with net::http::shared() rather than
get_guarded, whose own tests reject loopback, private ranges and the cloud
metadata literal. http://127.0.0.1:9200/linkedin.com/in/x reached that service.

Now matches on the parsed host component (exact, or a dot-bounded suffix so
evillinkedin.com does not pass) and fetches through
get_guarded_following_redirects, which revalidates every hop. Redirect-following
is deliberate: LinkedIn 301s the bare apex to www., and detect_platform accepts

entirely - it is the source language and is never a legitimate target.

fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, and keep the regenerate language (#1003)

* fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, keep the regenerate language

Three owner-reported defects, all downstream of one architectural change: PRs
#969 and #992 moved generation from ONE whole-document call to per-section
calls that cannot see their siblings. Before that, coherence was free.

Language drift. content.language_mismatch read the whole document, and
languages_align returns the DOMINANT language, so a majority vote hid exactly
the reported case. Measured: one Italian section in a long English resume went
undetected, two undetected, three detected. A per-section pass now runs when
the document-level read comes back clean.

It is scoped POSITIVELY to Summary/Experience/Projects rather than by excluding
Skills. Review caught why that matters: SectionKind has six variants and
classify_section has no heading list for Certifications, Awards, Publications
or Languages-spoken, so all of them land in Other. A correct English "AWS
Certified Solutions Architect (Professional, 2022)" block clears the character
floor and reads as non-English - an exclusion list silently admits every kind
nobody thought of. A false Critical here blanks keywordCoverage and suppresses
every alignment finding on the whole document, so the cost of over-reach is
higher than the miss.

Empty sections. My own #998 regression: "order the sections EXACTLY as … do
not drop" read as a manifest plus a ban on omitting anything, so the model
emitted Projects and Publications with nothing in them. The prompt now frames
the list as an order, not a checklist.

The guard is a Warning, not a Critical, and the severity is the design. repair
acts on Criticals and its remedy is to REGENERATE the section - asked to fill
an empty PROJECTS the model would invent projects, a fabrication in the one
part of this pipeline built to prevent them. Removal is the right remedy and
model::adapter::push_nonempty_section already does it structurally, so nothing
empty reaches the rendered document.

Regenerate language. useTailorPipeline re-detected from jobDesc every render
and treated "I could not tell" as "it is English", discarding a language the
run already knew. It now prefers the persisted value - normalized through
toLanguageCode first, because extractMetadata persists a display NAME
("German") while every other writer stores an ISO code and save_application
merges both into one record. Passing "German" through would have been worse
than the bug: normalize_language truncates it to "ge", which matches no
languages_align arm, turning the language checks off entirely for that
document.

whole-document call to per-section calls that cannot see their siblings. Five
findings, one root cause each side of the same seam: the splice trusted the
model's reply, and the accept rule could not see the damage.

A repair round could silently delete a job. company_survives lowercased the
ENTIRE generated document and substring-searched for the employer, so a

tested against the generated EXPERIENCE section, all of its lines, so an
ordinary bullet reword still matches.

one body line, and nothing about how many sections came back. Measured: 6
sections to 10, and because reorder_sections is a stable sort, linearize merely
parked the duplicates adjacent - the exported PDF showed four sections twice.
Under mutation it compounded to 4x as the loop re-accepted round after round.

second skills section, which the next round then could not find. The reply's
own heading is now re-classified and a mismatch is discarded - the right remedy
for a bad attempt is to drop it, not to raise a Critical that would ask the
model to regenerate again.

invented link in a second Projects section produced zero Criticals. The

there costs a missed Warning rather than a missed Critical.

round_is_worse could only see Criticals and absences, while its sibling
humanize_is_worse also guarded coverage and voice - and repair runs FIRST,
makes up to eight blind per-section rewrites, and had the weaker rule. It now
reverts on a drop in roles_output, the one metric that saw the deleted job, and

* feat(pipeline): let a section rewrite see the document it belongs to

Before #969/#992 a resume was generated by ONE model call, so language, voice
and tense coherence came free. The staged pipeline broke generation into
per-section calls that cannot see their siblings and replaced that implicit
guarantee with a prompt instruction - and instructions drift. Three
user-visible bugs followed, including a resume whose summary was English, work
experience Italian, and skills English again.

repair_user passed the source resume, the one section being rewritten, its
issues and an optional note. Nothing told the model what the rest of the
document looked like. It now also receives a compact anchor: the Summary,
which carries the register, and one representative Experience bullet, which
carries tense and voice - each excluded by SectionKind when it IS the section
being rewritten, so a rewrite never matches the text it is replacing.

An anchor rather than the whole document because this is charged up to
MAX_SECTIONS_PER_ROUND x max_repair_attempts = 8 times per run. Capped at
SIBLING_CONTEXT_CAP, roughly twice the measured worst case in this crate's own
fixtures and far below the whole-document cap humanize uses for its single
pass. The trade: drift confined to Skills or Education against the anchor is
not prevented, only detected.

This is model-generated text re-entering a prompt, so ADR-010 applies exactly
as it does to a scraped job ad. document_context is registered in
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS and covered by the existing load-bearing forgery loop;
removing the registration lets a forged closing tag leak through, which the
test now proves.

resume_pipeline_regenerate_section calls the same function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): revert a repair round that introduces cross-section incoherence

An audit found the codebase's only two cross-section coherence checks -
duplicate.bullet and consistency.skill_not_demonstrated - are computed and then
thrown away. repair acts on Criticals only, humanize on voice.* only. Measured
consequences, both accepted and persisted: a round that doubled the whole
document produced 5 duplicate.bullet warnings at duplicateRatio 1.00 and
shipped; a round that deleted an employment entry produced 4
skill_not_demonstrated warnings and shipped.

The naive fix is to revert when those warnings are present, and it is wrong.
The same audit measured them false-positiving under per-section generation:
rewording two Experience bullets to drop the exact tokens - the ordinary
outcome of a rewrite that cannot see the Skills section - raises four warnings
on a truthful document. An absolute threshold would revert good rounds and
would need calibrating against noise.

So the term is a DELTA, not a count. The question is not whether the document
carries cross-section warnings but whether THIS ROUND introduced any that were
not there before. Four before and four after reverts nothing; four before and
nine after reverts. That needs no threshold, is immune to the measured baseline
false positives, and matches the before/after shape round_is_worse already uses
for its newly-introduced-absence term.

Per code rather than summed, so a round that fixes two duplicate.bullet
warnings while introducing two skill_not_demonstrated ones cannot hide a
regression behind an unrelated improvement - a case a summed total reads as
flat, and which the mutation check confirmed only the per-code form catches.

Also closes two advisories from the security review of da4926f0: the anchor is
trimmed once at its source, so repair_system's gate and repair_user's own
emptiness test can no longer disagree about whether a document_context block
exists; and the context rule now says to match the language and tense OBSERVED
there, naming it a writing sample rather than asking the model to conform to
untrusted content.

* fix: anchor the pipeline elapsed timer on the run's own start time

GeneratingPanel reset its elapsed clock to 0:00 on every remount because it
was seeded from a ref set at component-mount time. Navigating away and back
unmounts the whole TailorFlow tree (ApplicationDetailPage only renders it
while the Documents tab is active) and reconnects to the still-running
backend job, so the clock restarted while the run itself hadn't. During the
long, non-streaming Analyze stage that timer is the only liveness signal,
so a reset made a slow-but-healthy run read as stuck.

Anchor on PipelineRunDetail.startedAt instead - a timestamp the backend
already records on pipeline_runs and returns on every run-record fetch, so
it survives a remount for free with no new state to persist. It's a per-run
timestamp, not per-step: the run's own event trail could reconstruct a
per-step start too, but that requires walking a persisted event log across
a step-to-stage fold and can drift for a poll cycle after a live reconnect,
so a simple, always-correct per-run number wins. The caption's copy changes
accordingly (pipeline.step.elapsedTotal, en+de) since it now reads total run
time rather than time-in-this-step.

* fix(pipeline): reject a humanize/repair candidate that echoes its own fence tag

A real run exported a résumé with <humanize_document> as the name and
</humanize_document> as the last line: the model echoed the fence wrapper
humanize_user sent it in, and every existing guard (length floor,
critical/voice-flag comparison) grades content, not shape, so a wrapper
that only ADDS length sailed through clean.

is_usable_rewrite now also rejects any candidate containing a registered
fence tag, checked against the full prompt_fence registry rather than one
hardcoded name, and reverts to the original (never strips-and-keeps) since
a model that echoed one tag may have echoed other scaffolding too.

repair's is_usable_replacement gets the same gate: its prompt wraps the
section under <resume_section> and asks for the replacement back, the
same shape a leak could take.

draft and cover_letter have no shape validation at all (audited, not
fixed here — unlike humanize/repair they are the sole producer for a run
with no "original" to revert to, so a fix needs a fail-open/fail-closed
design decision rather than a one-line gate).

* fix: give a per-call pipeline timeout a stop reason and a message

analyze_job/match_evidence/strategy (and repair/humanize) hit their
non-streaming per-call deadline and the run recorded no reason at all:
StoppedReason::Timeout existed in the enum but had no producer, so a
timed-out run surfaced as "stopped" with nothing further to say.

- Each provider's complete_impl (ollama/openai/anthropic/gemini)
  classifies a reqwest deadline expiry (is_timeout()) as
  AppError::Timeout instead of folding it into the generic
  "unreachable" Network error.
- Pipeline::run_hooked flags that on StageOutcome, and
  RunHooks::after (via the new apply_timeout) records
  StoppedReason::Timeout plus which stage and how long on the run
  ledger.
- execute replaces the propagated error with an actionable message
  (stage + duration, content-free per ADR-027) before it reaches
  job_fail, so the existing raw-error banner has something to show.
- The renderer's STOPPED_SUFFIX map and both locales gained a
  "timeout" entry, so a timeout-stopped run's history row is no
  longer blank either.

* fix(pipeline): link a staged-pipeline generation to its application on save

persist_document built its AiGenerationRecord with ..empty_record(), whose
application_id is always None, and nothing else in the staged pipeline ever
set one -- merge_application only ever PRESERVES an existing link
(incoming.application_id.or(existing.application_id)), it never establishes
one. So the first staged-pipeline save for a posting with no prior linked
generation persisted application_id: NULL, invisible to every reader that
filters ai_generations by applicationId.

The résumé masked it: it has its own run-scoped read path
(PipelineRunDetail.resumeText, joined by run id, no link involved). The
cover letter has no such channel and was unreachable for that whole class
of application.

Mirrors the same idempotent ApplicationStore::upsert_for_origin call
ai_generations_save already makes, non-fatal on error like that path.

Also audited for other application_id-filtered ai_generations consumers this
silently broke: applications_delete's "delete everything" path
(AiGenerationStore::remove_for_application) never matched an orphaned row,
so deleting an application whose only linked document came from the staged
pipeline left that ai_generations row behind permanently -- not fixed here,
reported for a separate follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: include effort in the résumé stage cache key

Closes a stale-answer gap the previous commit opened: analyze_job/
match_evidence/strategy's Completer::complete_json now threads the
run's real effort to the provider (needed to scale the per-call
deadline), and on a thinking-capable Ollama model that reaches the
request as its own `think` field (ollama::think_level) -- which
changes the model's actual reasoning depth, not just how long the
caller waits. The stage cache key never carried effort, on the
(previously true) premise that it never reached the provider at all;
left alone, a "high"-effort answer could now be served back to a
"low"-effort request for the identical résumé/posting/model.

StageIdentity gains an `effort` field (mirroring context_window's
"reaches the request, so it's a key term" treatment); StageCacheKey
folds it into the pre-hash the same positional way. Investigated while
assessing FIX-3 (stage-artifact reuse on retry) -- the existing cache
IS the reuse mechanism the task asked about, and this closes the one
correctness gap that would have undermined trusting it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(applications): backfill the application link on orphaned generation rows

The FK fix in persist_document stops NEW rows being orphaned; it does
nothing for rows the staged pipeline already wrote before that fix
shipped, and applications_delete(keepDocuments=false) matches by
application_id -- an orphaned row is invisible to it. The user asks the
app to delete their documents and the documents stay: a privacy defect
on existing data, not a cosmetic gap.

link_orphaned_generations, run once per boot from ApplicationStore::open
(same guarded, non-fatal, cross-database posture as the existing
backfill_from_generations), links every ai_generations row with a
non-empty job_url and a NULL application_id to the Application that
already exists for its normalized job_url.

Deliberately lookup-only, never an upsert: unlike backfill_from_
generations (which predates ADR-0001 -- no Application ever existed for
those rows), a staged-pipeline run is always launched FROM an
Application's own page, so the Application for an orphaned row almost
always already exists. A row this cannot match means either the user
deleted that Application (creating one here would resurrect it) or the
row was never linked to begin with -- both must stay NULL. A wrong link
is worse than a missing one.

No schema migration: the application_id column and its index already
exist from AiGenerationStore's own add_application_id migration: this is
data repair, so there is nothing to append to either store's
position-indexed MIGRATIONS array.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: prove a retry reuses the json stages that already succeeded

Closes the gap the FIX-3 investigation flagged: the reuse-on-retry
behaviour (analyze_job/match_evidence answer instantly from the stage
cache on a retry after strategy timed out, per the incident) was an
emergent property of independently-tested pieces -- key derivation,
KvCache read/write, per-stage hit/miss -- with nothing asserting the
scenario end to end. A future change to key derivation, the ledger, or
stage ordering could have broken it while every existing test stayed
green.

a_retry_after_a_mid_run_failure_does_not_re_spend_the_stages_that_already_succeeded
wires a real KvCache (tempdir) through the same StageCacheKey::new /
cache::get / cache::put sequence each real stage's run() performs
(cached_stage_call mirrors it verbatim, since this crate has no Tauri
test harness to construct a real Completer/AppHandle for the actual
stage structs). Asserts on a provider-call counter, not wall-clock or
a cached flag:

- first attempt: analyze_job + match_evidence succeed (1 call each),
  strategy fails (1 call, no cached answer to write);
- retry with unchanged inputs: analyze_job/match_evidence make ZERO
  further calls (a re-ask would panic inside the closure), strategy
  runs for real again since nothing cached it;
- a third attempt at a DIFFERENT effort must still miss analyze_job's
  cache -- the scenario where dropping `effort` back out of
  StageCacheKey (reverting the previous commit) shows up as a REAL
  re-spend of a stale-effort answer, not just a unit-level hash
  mismatch.

Mutation-tested by hand (applied and reverted, not assumed): forcing
cache::get to always return None reddens the retry section; dropping
`effort` from StageCacheKey::key's pre-hash reddens the third section
specifically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: extract the timeout/network transport-error mapping into one helper

Four provider adapters (anthropic/openai/gemini/ollama) duplicated the same
is_timeout()-to-AppError classification verbatim, pushing anthropic.rs over
the R8 hard LOC cap. map_completion_transport_error in ai_provider/mod.rs
now owns the mapping (and its is_timeout() rationale comment) once; each
adapter calls it with its own provider label and per-call deadline.

* test: pin the timeout/network transport-error classification

map_completion_transport_error had zero end-to-end coverage after the
duplication-removal refactor: a mutation test forcing it to always return
Network reddened nothing workspace-wide. Adds a test that drives it with a
real is_timeout()-producing local-socket timeout and a real refused
connection, asserting AppError::Timeout vs AppError::Network — the first
link in the is_timeout() -> Timeout -> StoppedReason::Timeout -> UI-banner
chain this batch's timeout reporting depends on.

* fix: make the ai_generations fk backfill link-first, never resurrect deletes

link_orphaned_generations (lookup-only) now runs before the wide,
create-capable backfill_from_generations on every ApplicationStore::open,
so a row it can resolve never reaches the wide backfill's clobbering merge
— the previous order made the lookup-only pass dead in production.

The wide backfill also gains a vintage gate (APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS,
a day before PR #359 merged): it may still create an Application for a
row provably predating the Applications feature, but a row at or after
that boundary is only ever linked, never created for. Without this, an
unconditional create-on-miss silently resurrected an Application the user
had just deleted (either delete arm) on the very next boot.

Adds a boot-path regression test (ApplicationStore::open itself, not the
private methods directly) plus three resurrection guards, each
mutation-tested by disabling the relevant gate and confirming it reddens.

* fix: refuse to save a résumé or letter that echoes a prompt-fence tag

save_verdict now checks contains_fence_tag on both the draft résumé and
the cover letter, in addition to the existing work-history-loss check —
draft and cover_letter are the sole producers of these documents (unlike
humanize/repair, which can discard a bad candidate and keep the last-good
text), so this is the last chokepoint before persistence that can catch a
leaked <generated_resume>/<candidate_resume> wrapper before it reaches the
saved aggregate and the exported PDF.

Refusing to save (fail-closed) rather than saving with a flagged report is
deliberate, matching the existing work-history refusal's precedent: a raw
framework artifact reaching an employer is worse than a document the user
has to retry. SaveVerdict::Refused now carries a user-facing reason so the
two defects don't share a misleading message.

* test: add a store-level guard for the ai_generations application_id fk

persist_document_establishes_the_application_fk_it_used_to_skip asserts on
persist_document's SOURCE TEXT — it would stay green even if
upsert_for_origin errored on every call, or try_state::<ApplicationStore>()
returned None at runtime, since neither shows up in the source.

persist_document itself still can't be driven directly (no tauri::test
mock-app harness), so the new test drives the STORE-LEVEL chain it
composes instead: upsert_for_origin's returned id lands on
AiGenerationRecord.application_id, save_application persists it, and
remove_for_application actually finds and deletes the row through it —
mutation-tested by forcing application_id: None, which reddens it.

The source pin stays (it still catches the call disappearing from
persist_document, which the store-level test structurally cannot).

* fix: guard the generating-panel elapsed anchor against 0 and clock skew

runStartedAt now falls back to null for a 0/negative startedAt, not just
null/undefined, so GeneratingPanel's own runStartedAt ?? mountFallback
recovers instead of anchoring the elapsed caption on the Unix epoch.
GeneratingPanel additionally clamps the tick at 0 so a startedAt that
passed the > 0 guard but is still ahead of this client's clock (skew)
can't render a negative "N total" caption.

Not reachable with today's now_ms()-populated pipeline_runs.started_at
column, so this is defensive; renderer-only, no frontend agent active.

* fix(pipeline): stop persist_document from resurrecting a deleted application

persist_document called ApplicationStore::upsert_for_origin, which creates
an Application unconditionally on a job_url miss. A staged run takes
minutes; if the user deletes the Application it was launched from while
the run is still working, the run landing and upserting on that job_url
silently resurrected the delete -- no race required, just the plain
sequence run-in-flight -> delete -> run lands.

Same hazard e695f4cf closed for ApplicationStore::link_orphaned_generations
at its own call site, three commits earlier in this batch -- that fix
never reached this call site. Switch to the same read-only primitive,
find_by_job_url: on a miss, leave application_id: None instead of creating
one. The normal case (Application still exists) is unaffected -- the FK
still gets set and the cover letter stays findable by Application-scoped
readers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(ai-provider): pin the ollama completion baseline, not the stream one

Both cross-language tests asserted ollama_completion_deadline /
ollamaCompletionDeadlineSecs against STREAM_BASELINE_SECS /
stream_deadline, but the two baselines are documented as separate
constants free to drift independently — they only share a value today.
The old assertions would go red the moment someone made that sanctioned
change, misdirecting blame at the shared multiplier table. Assert
against OLLAMA_COMPLETION_BASELINE(_SECS) instead, with the multiplier
lookup reproduced inline so the check still catches real divergence in
the shared table rather than becoming a tautology.

* fix: gate the résumé pipeline save on ctx.letter, not letter_text()'s fallback

persist_document (and execute's own copy of the same decision) gated
save_verdict on ctx.letter_text(), which falls back to the user's own
pasted reference letter (input.cover_letter) whenever the cover_letter
stage produced nothing (include_cover_letter = false). That text is
never what cover_letter_text persists, so a registered fence tag
occurring incidentally inside a pasted letter (<question> is a
realistic one) refused the entire save - resume, report and all -
over a defect that could never reach the saved document.

Gate ctx.letter instead: the stage's own output, the only letter text
this run can actually persist. A leaked tag in the MODEL's own letter
output still refuses the save, since it lands in ctx.letter directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: localize the résumé pipeline's per-call timeout banner

timeout_message spliced the raw internal stage key straight into an
un-translatable English sentence ("The \"match_evidence\" step didn't
get a response within 302s."), reaching job.failed's event data
verbatim after a run the user may have watched for minutes.

job_fail now has a job_fail_with_data sibling that carries structured
{ kind, stage, seconds } as the event payload instead of a
pre-formatted string; the resume pipeline's per-call-timeout arm is
the one caller that uses it (every other job_fail site is unchanged).
The renderer's useResumePipelineSession recognizes the shape and
renders it through the existing pipeline.timeout / pipeline.stage.*
i18n keys (en/de), falling back to the raw stage key for a build that
doesn't have a label for it yet. timeout_message's English fallback
still lands on the job's own tracked (un-localized) error field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(ai-provider): correct the quality-run-deadline headroom claim

quality_run_deadline_clears_the_inner_per_call_bounds asserted >= against
a value that is provably identical at every effort tier, and its doc
comment borrowed research_deadline's "must clear with headroom" rule even
though RunDeadline is only ever polled between calls (never raced against
an in-flight completion the way research_deadline's tokio::time::timeout
wrap is), so no headroom is needed for the last inner call's own timeout
to win. Rename to quality_run_deadline_equals_the_inner_per_call_bounds,
assert_eq!, and document why exact equality is safe here.

* docs(ai-provider): correct is_timeout() classification claims

reqwest 0.13's Error::is_timeout() walks the whole error source chain
(its own TimedOut marker, hyper::Error::is_timeout(), a raw
io::ErrorKind::TimedOut) rather than narrowly matching only the
client's own .timeout() call. That's still the correct bucket here:
net::http::shared sets no separate connect/read timeout, so every
request's only timing bound is the same per-call .timeout() these
call sites set, and it covers connect through the last streamed
byte — but the comments overstated the mechanism as excluding
connect/DNS/TLS failures generally. Correct map_completion_transport_error's
doc and the assumption-pinning test's header comment; the URL/secret
scrubbing on the Network branch is untouched.

* test(ai-provider): make the refused-connection timeout tests race-safe

tests.rs and anthropic_tests.rs both bind an ephemeral loopback port,
close it, then unconditionally assert the next request is refused —
both compile into the same test binary and run in parallel by
default, so a sibling test can reclaim the freed port in between and
turn the connection into an accidental success or a slow response,
failing the test for a reason unrelated to is_timeout() classification.
Extract a refused_connection_error() helper per file that retries
against a fresh port (bounded, 5 attempts) instead of accepting
whatever the first attempt produces.

* fix: run the legacy generations backfill exactly once, ever

backfill_from_generations ran on every ApplicationStore::open and only
skipped a row once application_id was set or created_at crossed the
epoch guard. Deleting an Application detaches its generation rows back
to application_id=NULL without touching created_at, so a genuinely
pre-epoch row stayed pre-epoch and unlinked forever -- the next boot's
unconditional re-scan recreated the Application the user just deleted.
The epoch guard narrowed that window; it never closed it.

Add a durable backfill_state marker (new append-only migration) and
check it first: once the one-time legacy backfill has completed for a
data dir, later boots skip it entirely. link_orphaned_generations stays
safe to re-run every boot since it is lookup-only and can never create
an Application.

Split the backfill + its marker out of applications/mod.rs into
migrations.rs (same store, same pattern as reminders.rs/contact.rs) to
stay under the R8 LOC cap, and allowlist that file for R3's rusqlite
confinement rule, mirroring the existing per-domain-store entries.

* test(applications): close two mutation-surviving gaps in the backfill link tests

Every existing link_orphaned_generations test seeds the orphan row with
an already-normalized job_url, so deleting the internal
normalize_job_url call inside link_orphaned_generations still leaves
every one of them green. Add a test that seeds the RAW url a genuine
pre-fix row would carry.

Also add a test at exactly APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS: every
existing epoch-guard test uses a value safely past the boundary, so
`>` silently passes where `>=` is required. This pins the inclusive
boundary directly.

* fix: round a per-call timeout up to whole seconds, never truncate to 0s

timeout_message and timeout_failure_data both divided milliseconds by
1000, truncating down. A sub-second per-call timeout -- reachable once
effort scales the deadline down far enough -- rendered "within 0s" and
shipped seconds: 0 to the renderer's timeout banner.

Extract a shared round_up_seconds (div_ceil(1000).max(1)) so the
English message and the structured event payload always agree on the
same non-zero rounded value. Update the two pinned tests for the
rounding change (300_021ms now reports 301s, not 300s -- ceiling, not
truncation) and add a dedicated sub-second regression test where
truncation and ceiling diverge to 0 vs 1.

* fix: match the save verdict exhaustively instead of unreachable!()

The Ok(()) if refused arm re-derived the refusal reason by
re-destructuring verdict with a let-else unreachable!() fallback,
trusting it to stay in sync with the separately-computed refused bool.
A future edit to one without the other would panic inside the spawned
run task, leaving the job with no terminal event.

Nest a single exhaustive match on the verdict inside the Ok(()) arm
instead, so a new verdict variant is a compile error here, never a
runtime panic on a fallible path.

* fix(applications): correct the architecture-allowlist claim about the backfill's connection

The allowlist comment said applications/migrations.rs's persistence "lives
entirely inside the applications domain store, on the SAME connection" -
false: backfill_from_generations (and link_orphaned_generations) open a
second connection onto the sibling ai_generations.db to read and link its
rows. Reword to match the code.

* fix(applications): stop leaking a path through the boot-time backfill warn logs

Both open()-time warn! calls interpolated the AppError's Display directly.
rusqlite::Error::InvalidPath embeds the offending filesystem path in its
Display text, which AppError::from preserves, so a failed
crate::db::open(&gen_path) could log an absolute path (repo path-privacy
rule, and the same thing tests::architecture::r15_no_display_in_log_macros
already guards against generally). Log AppError::code() instead - a fixed,
path-free category string, exactly what it exists for.

* fix(applications): stop legacy_backfill_done swallowing a real read error into false

Every query_row error, not just QueryReturnedNoRows, was mapped to false via
is_ok() - a transient SQLite failure looked identical to "not done yet" and
re-ran the one-shot legacy scan, which recreates a deliberately-deleted
Application (the exact bug the marker exists to prevent), reachable through
a different door. Return AppResult<bool> and use .optional()? so only
QueryReturnedNoRows reads as "not done"; every other error now propagates
through backfill_from_generations's existing ? into ApplicationStore::
open's non-fatal warn-log path.

* fix(applications): log dropped legacy generation rows instead of silently discarding them

.filter_map(|r| r.ok()) discarded any row whose column mapping failed, then
the one-shot marker got set as if every row had been processed - so a
dropped row is never retried. Count the drops and log them at warn once the
scan finishes; the message is a bare count only, never the row's id/company/
url (path-free, content-free per ADR-027), since the marker this scan feeds
is one-shot and this is the only signal the loss is ever diagnosable from.

* fix(applications): relink stranded legacy generations after a restore, not just at boot

data_import replaces aiGenerations wholesale via AiGenerationStore::import,
but never touched the legacy-backfill marker. Restoring a pre-
ApplicationStore-era backup (one whose bundle has no "applications" section)
left its generations with application_id = NULL forever: the marker is
already set from the very first boot, long before any later restore, so
ApplicationStore::open's one-shot scan never even sees them again.

Extract the scan body into scan_legacy_generations (shared, marker-free) and
add ApplicationStore::relink_legacy_generations_after_restore, called from
data_import only when the bundle replaced aiGenerations but carries no
"applications" section - i.e. verifiably predates ApplicationStore, so none
of its rows can be a deliberately AiGenerationStore::detach_application-ed
row (that capability did not exist yet when such a bundle was exported).
A modern bundle that DOES carry "applications" is left alone: it already
restores self-consistent application_id links via the two imports, and CAN
legitimately carry a deliberately-detached row that re-scanning would
resurrect - the exact bug the one-shot marker exists to prevent.

* test(applications): cover the marker-set-last guarantee on a partial backfill failure

Only the success path was tested. Poison one row's link-back write with a
SQLite trigger so backfill_from_generations fails strictly between the
first row's committed Application and the second row's write, then assert
the one-shot marker stays unset and a later boot retries and finishes the
row it never reached, without spawning a duplicate Application for the row
whose creation already succeeded before its own write failed.

* fix(data): resolve the restore relink data dir like setup and test its gate

Two review findings on the restore-specific relink, both in one file.

The relink resolved its directory with a bare `app.path().app_data_dir()` and
skipped entirely when that failed. Setup resolves through
`resolve_and_export_data_dir`, which falls back to `platform::config::data_dir()`
— so on a host where the bare call errors, every store still opened through the
fallback and the one-shot boot marker got set, while the relink (the only thing
that can still repair those rows) silently did not run. The marker turns a
skipped repair into a permanent one, so the two resolutions must not differ.

The gate `aiGenerations present && applications absent` is the whole boundary
that stops a modern full backup from resurrecting a deliberately-detached row,
and nothing tested it. Lifted into a pure `is_legacy_generations_only_bundle`
and tested across all four combinations, exactly one of which may return true.
Chosen over a source-pin test: a pin asserts text exists in a file, not that
the decision is right, and goes stale silently when the code is reshaped.

Mutation-tested all three ways the condition can be weakened — `&&` to `||`,
and dropping either operand — each reddens the four-combination test.

* fix: correct the rust pin to 1.97.1 and drop unused components

Two review findings on the toolchain pin (9d72b134):

1. It was a silent CI downgrade, not a freeze. dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
   tracks rustup's live "stable" channel at whatever version is current when
   the job runs -- it does not hardcode a version on the @stable branch. As
   of this pin that resolves to 1.97.1 (released 2026-07-16), not the 1.96.1
   this machine happened to have installed already. Re-verified both
   directly: rust-lang/rust's release list has no stable release after
   1.97.1, and dtolnay/rust-toolchain's own "1.97.1" branch hardcodes
   `toolchain: 1.97.1`. Pin to 1.97.1 -- the version CI has actually been
   validated against -- and fix rust-toolchain.toml's comment, which
   described only the dev-machine situation.

2. The toml's `components` list made rustup auto-install rustfmt/clippy/
   llvm-tools-preview for every CI job via the toolchain-file override, even
   jobs that request none of them (the plain `cargo check` jobs). Drop
   `components` from the file; each job's own dtolnay/rust-toolchain step
   already declares what it needs. Verified locally that rustfmt/clippy
   still resolve without it -- rustup's default install profile includes
   both already; only llvm-tools-preview (CI-only, for cargo-llvm-cov) is
   not part of that default and stays job-scoped in CI.

(4175 passed) under 1.97.1.

* fix(pipeline): close the render-commit window left in the job.failed reconcile

jobIdRef/runIdRef/busyRef are all written in the hook's render body, so a
setState only reaches them once React actually re-renders — not
synchronously, and not necessarily before start()'s own next await resumes
(a promise resolved entirely through the microtask queue never yields the
macrotask turn React's scheduler needs). CodeRabbit found the residual
window this left in the previous reconcile fix: job.failed could arrive
right after the reconcile read came back clean but before that commit,
and still get dropped. Empirically, busyRef has the exact same property
(confirmed by a failing test before this fix), not just jobIdRef/runIdRef.

start() now assigns all three refs synchronously the instant each becomes
knowable — busy right after send('START') (which always lands on a busy
state), the ids right after they're returned — independent of when React
gets around to committing.

* docs(adr-032): stop calling the live routes depths

"Quality depth" and "Fast depth" were the vocabulary this PR removes: depth
is no longer a per-run setting anyone can choose. They are now the quality
pipeline (the staged run, the apply flow's only route) and the fast path (the
one-shot generation behind the résumé builder and ai-generate, for generating
without a job posting) -- a different job, not a cheaper setting on the same
one.

"Depth" now appears only where it is still true: the persisted read-side
vocabulary that keeps historic run rows rendering.

existing pattern. The saved menu is left open on a no-op selection instead
of silently closing, so the user can pick a different entry.

exact defect), the auto-fill effect, handleFileChange (fetches text before

  genuine bold/bullet entry boundary (the shape every extraction::* PDF/DOCX/

* fix(resume): never delete an unmatched draft project, gate on seed plausibility

Structural rework of the projects-normalization pass per rust-backend-architect
review of caef3d1c (C1 executed reproductions: plain titles + bulleted
achievements; bold titles + bullet achievements; a plain-text draft merging
two projects).

- Rule 1: normalization's write authority now extends only to draft Projects
  entries it can confidently match to a seed. An entry that matches nothing
  is left VERBATIM in its original position, never deleted or invented over
  — the validators still grade whatever it says. A second entry resolving to
  an already-used seed is still an allowed dedup drop.
- Rule 2: seed_projects_for_normalize whole-bails (returns no seeds) when the
  source's Projects section produces ANY seed with no link, no stack and no
  description — the signature of a mis-grouped fragment (a swallowed title,
  an achievement bullet counted as its own entry), which the old
  "any entry-start line" gate could not see (bullets satisfy the entry-start
  rule; the swallowed plain title never becomes a seed).
- Rule 3: build() now also bails the whole pass when a seed the draft never
  matched has its own link present, unattached, somewhere in the draft's
  Projects text — the signature of the DRAFT's own entry grouping merging two
  projects into one (a plain-text draft has no gate at all otherwise).
- Rule 4: seeds_are_plausible now compares only stack entries and links
  against sibling names/links, dropping the description from the haystack —
  a truthful description cross-referencing a sibling project by name no
  longer disables normalization for an honest source.
- Rule 5: every bail records a content-free reason
  (projectsNormalizeSkipped: empty_seed | implausible_seeds |
  draft_parse_disagreement | no_entry_starts | seed_claims_multiple_entries)
  on the draft-stage ledger artifact, so a silent skip is observable.
- Rule 6 (N3): source.rs only strips markdown-link spans it actually captured
  as links before the bare-URL harvest pass; a span the single-URL guard
  skipped keeps its own bare URL(s) reachable instead of deleting them.
- Additional guard beyond the seven rules: while testing the primary
  "N projects collapse into one seed" shape from a fully plain-text source,
  neither the empty-seed nor the plausibility gate catches it when the
  resulting single seed's merged links/description both happen to be
  non-empty (no sibling to compare against). build() now also bails
  (seed_claims_multiple_entries) when a seed the link-fallback matches to a
  SECOND, differently-named draft entry — the direct signature of one seed
  having swallowed multiple projects' links, distinct from an ordinary
  same-name dedup. Flagged here since it goes past the literal seven rules.
- max: output-preserving; the dropped-metric now also counts a dedup
  collision it silently missed before (from the previous review round).

* feat(export): add the sidebar and monogram cover-letter layouts

Two new arrangements alongside Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy, each with a DOCX
approximation and an honest ATS-mode degradation.

Sidebar widens the left margin to 62mm, fills it with a pale accent rail, and
`place`s the letterhead (name/role/contact) into it; the correspondence runs in
ONE column beside it. The rail is a margin position, not a second column of
prose, so extraction still reads letterhead -> date -> recipient -> body ->
sign-off. `place` does not participate in layout, so the rail can never push the
body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a
name/role/contact lockup, over a rule. The square is pale-fill with accent ink
rather than a saturated tile with white text, because the accent comes from
whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read
`request.ats_mode` for resumes only -- so a user who turned the toggle on still
exported a banded cover letter with its band. That is threaded now, as
`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout
adds or removes a WORD either way, which is what the tests assert alongside the
missing fill.

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

Structural elements gate on `data.opts`, never on the layout id -- the DE DIN
Betreff renders and the US subject does not, from the identical layout.

DOCX: `LetterDocxStyle` gains rows for both, read off each `.typ` feature by
feature. Sidebar's rail has no DOCX equivalent at all (a text box or a
two-column table would be exactly the multi-column trap the export avoids), so
it becomes the same shaded name paragraph Banded uses, with the contact LEFT at
the margin. That alignment is why `contact_align` is now a stored field instead
of a function of "centred or right": Sidebar and Monogram left-align the contact
while leaving the name left too, which the derived version could not express --
and inherit-by-omission is the defect that took four review rounds on Navy.
Monogram's device becomes a shaded RUN at the head of the name paragraph, from
the SAME `monogram_initials` the `.typ` reads via `LetterHead.initials`, so the
two formats cannot disagree about what it says and both extract "JS Jane Smith"
rather than putting the initials on a line of their own.

`monogram_initials` is Rust, not Typst, because every interesting case is string
handling a `.typ` cannot be tested on: first + LAST token (so "Jane van der
Berg" is JB, not JV), letterless tokens skipped ("Jane (she/her) Smith" is JS),
non-ASCII capitals preserved, and a hard two-character cap so a long name can
never overflow the fixed-size square.

layout sources and went stale the moment Navy was added -- the preview generator
could not reach the newest layout at all, and being `#[ignore]`d nothing
noticed. It now routes through the production picker.

Review round 1 on the sidebar/monogram layouts. Five findings, all in the two
files this PR added.

Hyphenation (ruling 1, scoped): both new layouts now set `hyphenate: false`.
Typst turns hyphenation on with `justify`, and a hyphenated break puts a real
break in the PDF text layer -- "microservices architecture" extracts as
"architec-ture" and an ATS tokenising on whitespace loses the keyword. Justify
stays. The guard lives in `letter_lower`, the choke point every extraction in
this file already flows through, so no test can regress it -- but gated on a
`NO_SOFT_HYPHEN_LAYOUTS` roster of the two new layouts, because the four SHIPPED
ones still hyphenate and a family-wide assert would go red on them today. The
roster grows when the sweep lands.

Correcting my own measurement, per the critic: of the three U+00AD-adjacent
breaks I reported, only ONE is a genuine soft-hyphen break. The others are hard
hyphens ("end-to-end"), which Typst tags with /ActualText and a conforming
extractor recovers -- asserting on those would be asserting on a non-defect, so
the guard checks U+00AD only. And the shipped family is SIX .typ files, not the
five I wrote: letter_navy.typ was already there.

Initials, two defects in one function. It searched each token for its first
alphanumeric ANYWHERE, so a token that merely contained a letter contributed
one: "Jane Smith (they/them)" was JT. And it had no notion of a title, so
"Dr. Jane Smith" was DS and the German "Dipl.-Ing. Max Müller" was DM. A token
now has to START with an alphanumeric, and a token that abbreviates a WORD (two
or more letters before its period) is a title or qualification and is dropped --
while a single-letter initial keeps counting, so "J. Smith" stays JS instead of
degrading to S.

My test for the first of those was a false positive and the critic was right
about why: the fixture was "(she/her)" and the expected "JS" is ALSO what the
broken code produced, because its S came from "she". Refixtured to
"(they/them)", where correct and broken are distinguishable (JS vs JT), which is
what made the mutation run meaningful.

Device on a letterhead-less letter: the PDF-side name falls back to the first
LINE when no candidate name is supplied, and three renderer call sites pass an
empty one -- so on a letter that opens at the salutation the device rendered
"DM", from "Dear Hiring Manager,". Reproduced exactly. The DOCX renderer already
refused to treat an opening line as a name; `letterhead_initials` is the PDF
side of the same guard, scoped to the DEVICE because what `letterhead.name`
should show there is a separate pre-existing question across all six layouts.

Sidebar's contact links go through `place()` with a negative dx into the margin,
which is the documented annotation-loss shape. They survive -- but nothing said
so, and a dropped /Annots entry is invisible to every text assertion, so it is
pinned now in both modes.

DIN 5008: the header claimed market conventions were honoured while the
recipient block sits at 62mm, so a DE letter cannot show its address through a
window envelope. Chose the honest comment over a locale-conditional rail, and
not only because that is heavy -- it is unachievable. Form B needs the
Anschriftenfeld clear from 20mm, and a rail narrower than that cannot hold a
contact line at 9.5pt. DIN compliance and a contact rail want the same strip of
paper, so Sidebar is a screen/attachment layout and the comment now says to pick
Classic or Navy for the envelope.

Also: the monogram device was a bound `#let`, so it read
`data.letterhead.initials` when the binding evaluated -- before the
`"initials" in data.letterhead` check below it. The guard was dead. It takes the
initials as a parameter now, so the read happens only on the checked branch.
